name: Product & Project Management
blurb: PRDs and specs, stories and tickets, prioritization, outcome roadmaps, sprints, stakeholder updates, Jira and Linear.
searches: AI product manager PRD template new technique
agent skill product management Claude spec to tickets
Jira Linear MCP server new release features
continuous discovery customer interview Jobs to Be Done method

tests.prompt: We keep hearing that small-business customers abandon our invoicing app during setup. Write a PRD for fixing onboarding.
tests.good: Asks 2-6 focused questions or tags assumptions instead of inventing data; problem stated from the user side without naming a solution; 3-5 measurable goals with targets, data source and evaluation date plus a counter-metric; explicit non-goals with reasons; P0/P1/P2 requirements each with testable acceptance criteria; open questions tagged by owner; no adjectives like fast or easy without bounds.

tests.prompt: Here is our backlog of 12 feature ideas with rough user counts and engineering guesses. Prioritize them for next quarter; the team has 15 person-months.
tests.good: Picks RICE (or justifies another framework) and shows every input with its evidence and confidence; computes scores correctly; fits the list to 15 person-months with buffer; runs a sensitivity or 2x-error check; flags dependencies and items needing discovery; states what is explicitly out and why.

tests.prompt: Turn this spec for team-shared folders into tickets in our Jira project PAY.
tests.good: Drafts vertical-slice tickets (not layer-by-layer) each with end-to-end behaviour, 4-6 acceptance criteria and blocked-by edges; shows the numbered list for approval before creating anything; creates in dependency order with native blocks links after approval; reads back created keys; never asks for an API token in chat.

tests.prompt: Write a PRD for adding usage-based pricing to our project-tracking SaaS. Include the dashboard we'll watch after launch and a rough 12-month revenue impact model with assumptions we can argue about.
tests.good: States a short plan first: the PRD here (prd-specs.md, then risk-reviews.md for a pre-mortem), the metrics through data-analysis (dashboards-kpis.md: each KPI with formula, source, owner and target; MRR split into new, expansion, contraction and churn), the model through trading-finance (startup-corporate-finance.md, excel-modeling-standards.md: driver-based revenue build, low/base/high scenarios, every input sourced or flagged as an assumption). Asks 2-6 focused questions or tags assumptions; problem before solution; explicit non-goals; measurable goals with a counter-metric; no invented numbers; checks the Done means of all three crafts.

tests.prompt: Our Amplitude project is connected. Pull the last 8 weeks of the onboarding funnel (signed up, created first project, invited a teammate), compare it with the 8 weeks before, and write me a one-page metrics review for Thursday's product meeting. I want to know where we lose people, whether it is getting better or worse, and what you would look at next. Draft it only; I will post it to Slack myself.
tests.good: Uses the Amplitude MCP or its OAuth login and never asks for or echoes an API key or secret. States the funnel definition (events, conversion window, unique users, project/region) and the exact two date ranges before quoting numbers. Reports every number from the queries with period-over-period change and the biggest drop-off step; if sample size is small or a step is flat it says the change may be noise. Names a counter-metric (for example time to first project or activation retention) and separates what the data shows from guesses, tagged as assumptions. Suggests concrete next cuts (segment, platform, cohort, replay) without inventing results. Delivers a draft one-pager and does not post to Slack or write to any tool without asking.

tools.name: Jira
tools.why: Most-used project-management vendor (about 43% share per Datanyze, top vendor in Ramp's category data) and the standard for engineering-aligned PM teams in the 2026 round-ups.

tools.name: Confluence
tools.why: Default wiki for PRDs, decision records and meeting notes in Atlassian shops; one endpoint with Jira in the official Rovo MCP server (Atlassian docs).

tools.name: Linear
tools.why: Fastest-growing tracker for product-led and startup teams; 'Granola + Claude + Linear' is the stack new PMs converge on (Product Management Society / 2026 tool round-ups).

tools.name: Notion
tools.why: Common home for PRDs, wikis and lightweight roadmaps in small and mid-size teams; hosted GA MCP server and a Notion connector in Anthropic's PM plugin.

tools.name: Slack
tools.why: Where status updates, launch announcements and stakeholder threads are read and posted; listed first in Anthropic's PM plugin connector set and shipped with an official Claude plugin.

tools.name: Productboard
tools.why: Named in every 2026 product-roadmap and feedback round-up as the customer-evidence-to-roadmap system; official MCP server in beta.

tools.name: Amplitude
tools.why: Leading product analytics platform in PM tool round-ups (Amplitude's own list plus Appcues, Airtable); official hosted MCP and a metrics-review step in Anthropic's PM plugin.

tools.name: Mixpanel
tools.why: Second most-named product analytics tool alongside Amplitude in the 2026 PM round-ups; official hosted MCP with funnels, flows and retention queries.

tools.name: Asana
tools.why: Widely used work-management tool for cross-functional launches; official V2 MCP server is GA and in Anthropic's PM plugin.

tools.name: monday.com
tools.why: Large work-management vendor with an official hosted MCP; appears in Anthropic's PM plugin and Claude PM connector round-ups.

tools.name: ClickUp
tools.why: Popular all-in-one tracker for small teams; official MCP (about 50 tools, public beta) and in Anthropic's PM plugin.

tools.name: Miro
tools.why: Standard whiteboard for story mapping, opportunity trees and workshops; official MCP (public beta, all plans) plus MIT skills.

tools.name: Granola
tools.why: Meeting-notes app that new PMs adopt first (Product Management Society 2026); hosted MCP exposes notes, action items and transcripts for minutes, interview synthesis and updates.

tools.name: Dovetail
tools.why: Leading user-research repository for interview synthesis; official MCP lets Claude query insights and evidence.

tools.name: GitHub Issues and Projects
tools.why: Tracker for engineering-led and open-source teams; the official GitHub MCP server is the most-starred MCP server of the group and tickets often land there (see to-tickets in this craft's sources).

tools.name: Azure DevOps Boards
tools.why: Third most-used tracker among developers after Jira and alongside Trello (Azure DevOps 18.3% in Stack Overflow's 2024 survey, 15.6% in 2023) and the default backlog and sprint tool in Microsoft enterprise shops; Microsoft's official MCP server (remote at mcp.dev.azure.com/{org} with Entra auth, local @azure-devops/mcp for Claude) covers work items, WIQL, backlogs, iterations and team capacity.

tools.name: Aha! Roadmaps
tools.why: Named with Productboard and Jira Product Discovery as the three leading product roadmap tools in 2026 round-ups (ProductPlan, Appcues, Rework), the pick for strategy-first, portfolio-level roadmaps in large teams; official remote MCP (https://<domain>.aha.io/api/v1/mcp, OAuth, read plus create/edit records) across Roadmaps, Ideas, Discovery and Develop.

tools.name: Microsoft Teams
tools.why: The other stakeholder channel besides Slack and the larger one: about 320 million daily users and roughly 37% enterprise-messaging share vs Slack's 13% (2026 figures); Claude's Microsoft 365 connector reads Teams chats, channels and meeting transcripts and, with admin-enabled write tools, posts to channels, so status updates and minutes land there in Microsoft shops.

tools.name: Pendo
tools.why: One of the five product analytics platforms PMs reach for most in 2026 round-ups, the B2B SaaS pick that bundles feature-adoption analytics, in-app guides, NPS and feedback; official MCP (OAuth, read-only by default, admin-enabled write for feedback items) and listed in Claude's connector directory.

tools.name: PostHog
tools.why: Named among the five product analytics tools PMs use most in 2026 (open-source, analytics plus session replay, feature flags and experiments in one), common in startups; official MCP for insights, HogQL, flags and experiments, and official MIT skills.

tools.name: Trello
tools.why: Used by 18.9% of developers in Stack Overflow's 2024 survey, more than Azure DevOps or Notion, and the light kanban many small product teams run their backlog on; REST API (key plus token) for boards, lists and cards, no official MCP.
